# Marten 2.0 (`marten_20`) — spec sheet

*Generated by `tools/specsheet/build_roster.py` from `tools/specsheet/roster_inputs.py`; edit the inputs, not this file.*

| Class | Archetype | Durability | Base price |
|---|---|---|---|
| Compact | early-90s European FF hot hatch, 2.0 L 16-valve naturally aspirated I4 | 2 / 5 | 9,500 |

## Design note

The original-recipe hot hatch: a big, torquey 2.0 in a small hatch shell. Where the Vireo needs revs, the Marten pulls from 3000 rpm in any gear, so it is quicker away from junctions and easier to drive fast — at the cost of torque steer under full throttle in the low gears. A soft front and a stiff rear bar make it tuck in and rotate on a lift; leave the throttle planted and it understeers.

## How this car breaks

90s unibody with short crumple rails: a moderate nose hit reaches the radiator and the transverse engine quickly, and in Simulation one committed frontal at speed ends it. The doors have no real intrusion beams, so side hits reach the cabin early. Plastic bumpers and a steel hood crumple at parking speeds, but every panel is cheap and bolts back on.

## Sources (type)

- manufacturer spec-class data for early-90s European 2.0 L FF hot hatches (mass, dimensions, gearing)
- road-test figures for the class (0-100, braking, skidpad)
- engineering tables (tire radius, ride frequency, caliper hydraulics)

All values are class-typical figures for the archetype, rounded; no single real vehicle is reproduced.

## Inertia

Box approximation about the CG, scaled for mass concentration (`k < 1`: mass near the centre, e.g. mid-engine; `k → 1`: mass at the ends):

```
I_roll  = k_r · m·(W² + H²)/12
I_pitch = k_p · m·(L² + H²)/12
I_yaw   = k_y · m·(W² + L²)/12
```

| Axis | Box (kg·m²) | k | `inertia_kgm2` |
|---|---|---|---|
| roll | 450 | 0.80 | 360 |
| pitch | 1705 | 0.90 | 1530 |
| yaw | 1792 | 0.92 | 1650 |

## Engine

2.0 L DOHC 16-valve I4, naturally aspirated, multi-point injection. Class-typical early-90s European 2.0 16-valve (~55 kW/L, 110 kW at 6000 rpm, ~180 N·m at 4600) per manufacturer spec-class data; a broad, flat curve rather than the Vireo's cam-step.

Peak **112 kW @ 6500 rpm**, **180 N·m @ 4600 rpm**. Idle 850 / redline 6800 / limiter 7100 rpm. Rotating inertia 0.12 kg·m² (class: 0.10 small four … 0.30 big-block). Engine braking 12% of peak torque = 22 N·m. Power-to-weight 101 kW/t.

## Drivetrain

5-speed close-ratio manual, open front differential. Layout **FWD**; front diff: open; rear diff: open. Clutch capacity 1.40 × peak torque = 250 N·m. Shift time 0.40 s.

| Gear | Ratio | Overall | km/h @ redline |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 3.45 | 13.59 | 53 |
| 2 | 2.13 | 8.39 | 85 |
| 3 | 1.48 | 5.83 | 123 |
| 4 | 1.12 | 4.41 | 162 |
| 5 | 0.89 | 3.51 | 204 |

Final drive 3.94, reverse 3.39. Speeds use the driven-wheel loaded radius 0.279 m.

## Suspension

Springs from ride frequency, `k = m_s·(2πf)²` with sprung corner mass `m_s = axle load/2 − unsprung`; dampers `c = 2ζ·√(k·m_s)`, ζ = 0.30 bump, rebound = 1.5 × bump.

| Axle | m_s | f | Wheel rate k | Bump c | Rebound c | Travel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Front | 327 kg | 1.60 Hz | 33100 N/m | 1980 N·s/m | 2970 N·s/m | 0.15 m |
| Rear | 196 kg | 1.75 Hz | 23700 N/m | 1290 N·s/m | 1940 N·s/m | 0.16 m |

Round 12b ride rule (A): the file carries the derived dampers × 1.2 bump / × 1.6 rebound (rebound ≈ 2 × bump), after any tunes below: **2380 / 4750 N·s/m F, 1550 / 3100 N·s/m R** (bump / rebound).

Anti-roll bars from a roll-gradient target of 2.8°/g with 45% of roll stiffness at the front. Roll arm h − h_rc = 0.395 m (roll centres 0.08 m F / 0.12 m R). Required total K_φ = m·g·arm/φ = 88327 N·m/rad; springs give k·t²/2 = 33842 F / 23862 R N·m/rad; bars supply the rest as `arb_n_per_m = K_bar/t²` = **2900 F / 12300 R N/m** (clamped at ≥ 0). Resulting gradient 2.8°/g, front share 45%. Bump stops 150000 N/m.

Alignment: camber -0.8° F / -1.0° R, toe +0.00° F / +0.15° R (+ = in), caster 3.5°.

## Brakes

Full-pedal line pressure 100 bar.

- Front: 280 mm disc, pistons per side 54 mm → A = 22.9 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 115 mm, pad μ = 0.38: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.38·100 bar·22.9 cm²·0.115 m = **2002 N·m**
- Rear: 245 mm disc, pistons per side 34 mm → A = 9.1 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 98 mm, pad μ = 0.38: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.38·100 bar·9.1 cm²·0.098 m = **673 N·m**

Lock check at 1 g on μ = 1 (load transfer m·a·h/L): front needs 1250 N·m/wheel (capacity 1.60×), rear needs 277 N·m/wheel (capacity 2.42×).

`wp_vehicle` gives the axle `bias_front` favours its full `max_torque_*` and scales the other by (1 − b)/b, so `max_torque_*` holds the caliper capacity per wheel and `bias_front` acts as the proportioning valve: the rear is trimmed to the same lock margin as the front (ideal rear = T_f · lock_r/lock_f = 444 N·m), never boosted above its caliper capacity. Rear capacity exceeds that, so `bias_front` = T_r/(T_r + ideal) = **0.602** → delivered 2000 N·m front / 443 N·m rear per wheel at full pedal. Handbrake 870 N·m per rear wheel.

## Steering

Ratio 15.5:1. Kerb-to-kerb turning circle 10.4 m → outer-front path radius 5.10 m, rear-axle-centre radius 3.75 m → mean road-wheel lock δ = atan(L/R) = **0.582 rad (33.4°)** (outer 29.0°, inner 39.1° at full Ackermann; `ackermann_frac` 0.70). Rack speed 1.5 rad/s.
